seoTitle: CSV Column Splitter: One Column into Several by Separator
metaDescription: Split a CSV column on a comma, space, slash or other separator into new columns with names you choose. Free and private.
intro: Splits one column into several parts, for example Smith, John into surname and first name, leaving all other columns where they are.
why:
Names, addresses and codes often arrive packed into one column. Splitting on the separator gives you sortable, filterable fields.

Set a maximum number of parts so extra separators stay in the last part, such as middle names. Name the new columns or let the tool call them name_1, name_2. Rows with fewer parts get empty cells. The original column can be kept or removed.
howTo: Paste the CSV with a header.
Enter the column and the separator text.
Set a maximum number of parts and optional new names.

faq.q: Can the separator be several characters?
How do I split on a tab?

faq.a: The CSV is parsed first, so commas inside quotes are not column breaks, but your separator still applies inside the cell.
Yes, each part is trimmed of surrounding spaces.
